anomalies.observed: On the DISPLAY sheet (display.kicad_sch, page 5) the SSD1306 module U1 pin 28, whose symbol name is 'VCC', is wired directly to a GND power symbol. The 2.2 uF decoupling capacitor (C8) and the VCC arrow are instead placed on pin 9 (VDD).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the VCC pin is the chip's supply pin that must sit on the board VCC rail: 'C7 (2.2 µF) — U4 VCC (digital-logic supply pin) to GND' and 'U4's VBAT pin ... is tied directly to the board's main VCC net'. A pin named VCC should connect to the VCC net, not to ground.

evidence.quote: display.kicad_sch, page 5: U1 (ER-OLED0.96-1W) left column top pins 9 VDD -> VCC arrow, 8 VSS -> GND, 25 VLSS -> GND, 28 VCC -> GND arrow
C7 (2.2 µF) — U4 VCC (digital-logic supply pin) to GND

anomalies.impact: The SSD1306's VCC supply pin is shorted to ground, so the display driver's analog/charge-pump supply is held at 0 V. The OLED will fail to initialize or light; if VCC and VDD are internally common on the die this also pulls the VCC rail toward ground.

parsed.summary: Most of the build matches the specification (NFC I2C pull-ups, SSD1306 I2C BS-pin strapping, TSC series-R / sampling-C, SWD connector, decoupling values), and the systematic reference-designator shift (U2->U3, U3->U4, U4->U1, J1->J2, A1->A2, A2->A3) is only a relabeling, not a behavioral fault. The one deviation the drawing supports is the display module's pin 28 (VCC) being tied to GND instead of the VCC rail, which is a supply pin shorted to ground.
